answer: Paired-Identity Merge Right** Each identity carries a unique signal derived from its registration history. When two identities ever act on the same resource (a shared payment channel, a common upstream), the protocol forces a merge: both histories combine into one, and duplicate rights collapse to a single share. The cost is that N clones yield the same total claim as one honest identity, so cloning pays nothing while each extra registration still consumes real setup effort. A river of merged records makes duplication self-defeating; cedar-stable identities gain from clean lineage.
